evidence.claim: plantation buildings

evidence.claim: Western York County’s byway connects Kings Mountain National Military Park, York and a chain of towns ending at Smyrna.
evidence.quote: that portion of South Carolina Highway 97 from South Carolina Highway 211 to North Main Street in the Town of Smyrna

evidence.claim: The county lies in the Piedmont, with a predominantly rural western sector and heavily wooded areas.
evidence.quote: All of York County is within the piedmont region. Although heavily wooded in many rural areas and retaining a predominantly rural character in its western sector

evidence.claim: South Carolina’s designation defines one contiguous route of approximately 57 miles, including side roads toward Brattonsville and along York Street in Sharon.
evidence.quote: all being one contiguous route of approximately fifty-seven miles, is designated as the Western York County Scenic Byway.

evidence.claim: including side roads toward Brattonsville
evidence.quote: including approximately one and eight-tenths mile of a side road known as Brattonsville Road

evidence.claim: along York Street in Sharon.
evidence.quote: including approximately one-fourth mile of a side road known as York Street

evidence.claim: The byway became law on June 3, 2009.
evidence.quote: HISTORY: 2009 Act No. 51, SECTION 1, eff upon approval (became law without the Governor's signature on June 3, 2009).

evidence.claim: Its designation joined sections of existing state roads and directed the Department of Transportation to install identifying signs.
evidence.quote: (B) The Department of Transportation shall install appropriate markers or signs to implement this designation.

evidence.claim: The Brattonsville side road was explicitly included, making the historic district part of the designated corridor rather than an unrelated attraction.
evidence.quote: including approximately one and eight-tenths mile of a side road known as Brattonsville Road

evidence.claim: From Kings Mountain, SC 161 leads toward York.
evidence.quote: That portion of South Carolina Highway 161 from Kings Mountain National Military Park near the Bethany community to South Carolina Highway 49 in the City of York

evidence.claim: Through York, the route uses sections of SC 49 and SC 5, then SC 324 and S-46-347 toward SC 322.
evidence.quote: that portion of South Carolina Highway 324 from South Carolina Highway 5 to S-46-347, that portion of S-46-347 from South Carolina Highway 324 to South Carolina Highway 322

evidence.claim: The Brattonsville excursion comes before McConnells and Bullock Creek.
evidence.quote: that portion of South Carolina Highway 322 from South Carolina Highway 347 through the Town of McConnells to South Carolina Highway 49 in the Bullock Creek community, including approximately one and eight-tenths mile of a side road known as Brattonsville Road

evidence.claim: Continue to Sharon, then take the corridor through Hickory Grove to its end at North Main Street in Smyrna.
evidence.quote: that portion of South Carolina Highway 211 from South Carolina Highway 49 to South Carolina Highway 97 in the Town of Hickory Grove, and that portion of South Carolina Highway 97 from South Carolina Highway 211 to North Main Street in the Town of Smyrna

evidence.claim: Through York, the route uses sections of SC 49 and SC 5
evidence.quote: that portion of South Carolina Highway 49 between Kings Mountain Street and Liberty Street in the City of York, that portion of South Carolina Highway 5 from Congress Street to South Carolina Highway 324 in the City of York

evidence.claim: Continue to Sharon
evidence.quote: that portion of South Carolina Highway 49 from South Carolina Highway 322 in the Bullock Creek community to South Carolina Highway 211 in the Town of Sharon

evidence.claim: Patriots defeated American Loyalists at Kings Mountain on October 7, 1780, destroying the left wing of Lord Cornwallis’s army.
evidence.quote: The Battle of Kings Mountain was fought on October 7, 1780, and destroyed the left wing of Lord Cornwallis' army

evidence.claim: The victory stopped the British advance into North Carolina and forced Cornwallis to retreat from Charlotte into South Carolina.
evidence.quote: The victory halted the British advance into North Carolina, forced Lord Cornwallis to retreat from Charlotte into South Carolina

evidence.claim: Congress established the military park in 1931 to commemorate the battle.
evidence.quote: Kings Mountain National Military Park was established on March 3, 1931 by an act of Congress

evidence.claim: Its paved battlefield trail follows Patriot positions at the mountain’s base and climbs to the crest where the Loyalists stood.
evidence.quote: A one and a half mile paved trail leads from the visitor center around the base of the mountain along the Patriot lines and ascends to the crest where the Loyalists were positioned.

evidence.claim: Along it are monuments and Patrick Ferguson’s grave.
evidence.quote: The trail passes several monuments, large and small, the earliest dating from 1815, as well as Patrick Ferguson's grave

evidence.claim: Patriots defeated American Loyalists
evidence.quote: a pivotal and significant victory by American Patriots over American Loyalists

evidence.claim: Clapboards cover the original logs of Brattonsville’s Revolutionary House, built by William Bratton in 1776 as a single room with a small porch.
evidence.quote: The Revolutionary House, built in 1776 by Colonel William Bratton (who fought in the Revolutionary War), was originally a one-room log house with a small porch. Later additions were added to the original structure, and clapboard siding was placed over the original logs.

evidence.claim: The family’s later Homestead was the center of an 8,500-acre plantation.
evidence.quote: was significant as the center of an 8500-acre plantation.

evidence.claim: The history here also includes Watt, a man enslaved by the Bratton family who supplied intelligence to Patriot forces before Huck’s Defeat.
evidence.quote: With intelligence provided by John McClure's younger sister, Mary, and a Bratton family slave named Watt, the loosely organized Patriot forces swarmed after Huck.

evidence.claim: Historic Brattonsville operates as an open-air museum.
evidence.quote: operates as an open-air museum.

evidence.claim: Its buildings include the McConnell House, moved here in 1983, as well as the Homestead and Hightower Hall.
evidence.quote: Buildings include Hightower Hall, The Homestead, and the McConnell House (moved to the site in 1983).

evidence.claim: The W.L. Hill Store brought the scale of a city department store to York Street in Sharon.
evidence.quote: its size and grandeur was meant to mimic larger stores in major cities.

evidence.claim: Built in 1913 to a design by Julian Starr, the three-story building is part of the Hill Complex Historic District.
evidence.quote: The W.L. Hill Store, built in 1913, is an historic three story department store located on York Street in the town of Sharon

evidence.claim: That district also includes William Lawrence Hill’s house, cotton gin, and cotton warehouse and dock, placing the store among the buildings of his broader enterprise.
evidence.quote: The buildings are the William L. Hill House (c. 1890), W. L. Hill Cotton Gin (c. 1925), W. L. Hill Cotton Warehouse and Dock (c. 1920), and the separately listed W.L. Hill Store (1913).

evidence.claim: Sharon’s separate downtown historic district preserves a group of mainly masonry commercial buildings dating from 1908 to 1944.
evidence.quote: The buildings are predominantly masonry commercial buildings built between 1908 and 1944.

evidence.claim: to a design by Julian Starr
evidence.quote: Designed in the commercial style, by locally prominent architect Julian Starr

evidence.claim: part of the Hill Complex Historic District.
evidence.quote: It is located in the Hill Complex Historic District.

evidence.claim: his broader enterprise
evidence.quote: The buildings are commercial, industrial, and residential buildings built by William Lawrence Hill

evidence.claim: The park also marks the end of the Overmountain Victory National Historic Trail, which commemorates the Patriot army’s approach over the Appalachian Mountains.
evidence.quote: The park is the terminus of the Overmountain Victory National Historic Trail commemorating the route of the Patriot army from over the Appalachian Mountains to the battle.

evidence.claim: At Hightower Hall, the property includes two cabins that housed enslaved people.
evidence.quote: Also on the property are two barns and two slave cabins.

evidence.claim: The store itself received National Register recognition in 1995, before the wider Hill district was listed in 2003.
evidence.quote: On January 20, 1995, it was added to the National Register of Historic Places.

evidence.claim: the wider Hill district was listed in 2003.
evidence.quote: It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2003.

Sharon town article places Hill’s Mercantile at the turn of the 19th/20th centuries; store-specific 19.txt and district 20.txt both give 1913, used here.
Kings Mountain trail-access improvements in 23.txt are future-tense and undated. No completion, accessibility or current operating arrangements claimed.
Brattonsville ownership phrasing in 16.txt is unclear and not reused. Enslavement is documented via Watt in 17.txt; no unsupported visitor programming claimed.
No motifs fields supplied in current; story motifs set to an empty array. Brattonsville scene uses town for the built historic site rather than unsupported prairie.
